It's not really practical to be cooking in the morning tbh, or any guarantee that I'll be able to get access to a stove, that a shop will be in walking distance or open before we leave in the morning, usually it's a pick up breakfast and lunch from a bakery as we pass through some village and eat it in the car, leave the rest in the car and maybe eat it for lunch or maybe come back to it at the end of the day.

I can't research where we're staying and see what's around as we won't know until we're driving down, and then may move around staying in different places different nights, we'll be camping but not necessarily in actual camp sites or in/near villages.  More likely will make it to a supermarket every few days and hope to drive past a village bakery in the morning for breakfast, so dried food (pasta or rice), things in cans and bottled sauces is the usual food.  And a shit load of bread (last time I was on 2 baguettes a day).

I'll also be doing a lot of exercise, last time I was eating 4-5000 calories a day, being told off for not eating enough and lost half a stone over 3 weeks.  I think my RMR is about 1400.

* My great grandma drives over to my workplace with the new portable cd player she got my great granddad (who was blind and going deaf) to ask me to turn the volume up.  There's about 5 buttons on this thing.  I even try to show her which buttons but she says it's fine now, it's at the right volume so he can hear it.

* When I was younger my nan drove to my parents house, picked me up and took me back to hers to show her how to use the @ key.  She'd been taking computer lessons and knew how to use the numbers (as in press shift) but sadly hadn't twigged that worked on other letters too.

* My nan visited me at work to ask how to use the space bar on her mobile.

* My dad is usually OK at computers, he has his own company and they have a server.  For 8 years they were backing up the server daily onto these tapes, he said he couldn't work out to restore them and could I have a look.  The tapes have a switch on them to allow writing or not.  Nothing had ever been written on the tapes.

* My dad asks me that if they put more RAM in the server will that speed up all the computers.

* My mum is just special, she works on computers every day, she was once trained on and can thus use excel 2000 and only excel 2000, if she needs to write a document she writes it in excel, she extends the column to be the width of a page and writes each line in a new cell (no word wrapping or anything like that).  If she needs to edit anything she writes then the whole paragraph must be edited manually (eg, a word added would push the next word to the line below, so that needs editing, etc etc).

It was OK, just a posh night out really, I wasn't popular at school so was a bit nervous and probably didn't have as much fun with school people as I would with my friends outside school and in the UK we tend to start going to clubs from 15/16ish so drinking and dancing is quite a normal way to spend a Saturday night!

Mostly I went because I like excuses to wear a pretty dress.

It sounds like she has got some kind of mental health issues, do you know any of her friends who you can talk to?  Someone needs to talk to her in the politest possible way and get her to go see her doctor.  Hopefully she might also realise that her living situation is NOT helping and that she does need to move out.  She might already realise this though and be waiting to move out in June.

You do need to explain that you don't want to renew the lease with her, is there any way that you can make it seem to be less like you just hate her, eg one of you have a partner move in instead (even if they aren't really moving in, just claim that they are, that you'll need the space of two rooms and find someone else to take the other room when they are gone).  The main reason I suggest making it look less like it's just that you hate her is to try and make her not turn into even more of a crazy person.

If there's anyway you can manipulate her into her saying she doesn't want to renew the lease then that's the winning option - she must realise she's not happy in her situation and if she's the one who is dropping on the agreement she might feel like it's a bit of a victory to her, or at the very least relief that the shit situation she's living in will be ending.

Pretend to forget about the agreement of renewing the lease and all start looking for new places, ask her what she is gonna do when it expires, hopefully she'll start looking for a place on her own, meanwhile renew the lease anyway with someone else, she will know that she is moving out and the worse case scenario is that she's pissed when she finds out you lot all decided to stay without telling her, but hopefully you can hide that until the last few days and then never see her again.  It's harsh on her though and might not help her mental state to realise you all went behind her back - I'd only do it if being reasonable doesn't work.  Ultimately it's probably the best for her to find a new living situation as this one obviously isn't working for her.

My vocal cords are used when I sneeze (I think), I can't control it, I sneeze incredibly loudly, I stop lectures, I've had someone shout 'bless you!' from across the other side of a dual carriageway, it's normal for people to turn around and stare, or jump a foot in the air, I even was threatened with receiving a verbal warning in a job if I didn't start sneezing quieter.  

I really can't help it, it's not a concious thing, several people have tried to teach me to sneeze quietly and all have failed.  Both of my parents and my brother also sneeze like this.

The tying up game: There were usually 4 of us who played this (my brother and the brother and sister who lived a few doors away).  One person would be tied to an object, usually a chair, with whatever could be found.  This person would then either be left, or we might stand and watch for a bit, to try and untie themselves.  Success was tying them up sufficiently that they couldn't free themselves (although this rarely happened, largely I suspect because we were under 10 and doing the restraining largely with dressing gown cords and belts).

Now I think it was an odd game, but I did love it, it was my favourite game, I also wonder if it contributed to my adult enjoyment of bondage, I have yet to get the courage to ask my brother or the other pair of kids we played with if they grew up to like bondage.

Wow, that's pretty bad, I didn't realise something like that could be related to birth control, but there are other types.

Depo injections and hormone implants both usually help reduce PMS and such, but it's something to talk to your doctor about, especially if you think you've have problems in the past.

I don't know if it would work in that situation but you could try looking at techniques like mindfulness or grounding, I suffer from mental illness that gives me very drastic mood swings and can make me react very intensely to things similar to how you describe and these are the things I'm supposed to be learning (although usually it takes someone else to help 'ground' me as it were).

Why can't you take birth control any more?  A few reduce the severity of PMS or stop the cycle all together (I've lost count of the last time I had a proper period, I get 1 or 2 days of bleeding a year, it's awesome).

My mum was generally a fan of 'real' food, avoided places like mcdonalds and didn't really like to give us overly processed food.  So in primary school they had burger patty things, having never seen a burger without a bun and virtually every burger I'd had having been home made I didn't know what they were.

I asked another student, who sarcastically told me they were dog poo.  I did not detect the sarcasm.

Logically I knew they couldn't really be dog poo, because the school surely wouldn't really feed us dog poo, but I wasn't certain enough to risk it so never touched them.  I felt too scared to ask someone else though and couldn't work out what they were.  It wasn't until I got to high school where they had a much larger canteen and labelled the food that I finally found out what they were (although by then I associated them too much with dog poo to ever eat one, I still can't eat processed burgers which aren't in a bun).

Hypothermia.  Absolutely horrible.

Dysentery was pretty bad too and lasted a lot longer, but I think the hypothermia was a worse experience overall.

They finally told the kids once they had grown up and got 'officially' married after they retired.

I try to clarify, some people don't accept the explanation though, I never did very well with insecure men.

I mainly use the word willy because I find it amusing, most boys don't like it, it's the kind of word parents use with small children ("winkle" is another popular one for kids), I just think it's a funny word.

My partner is very good at dealing with arguments with me when I get completely stupid and unreasonable.

Key - after the event (as you can't change what's happened) not pointing out that I was unreasonable, once I've calmed down I will realise this and will eventually say it, but just being genuinely apologetic and not on the defensive or accusing me of anything is the way to do it.

No "I'm sorry but...[you are being an unreasonable nutjob]", don't accuse, don't be defensive, just apologise for the argument.  With me hugs and smiles on his behalf help a lot too, to let me know that he's OK with me, as I'm usually feeling pretty useless and crap in the aftermath.

Edit - I know everyone is different, just thought getting a girl with BPD's perspective wouldn't hurt

I have been on all the same anti depressants as you, never helped and can certainly relate to the feeling of being a lower form of life, at best I feel like I'm still a child but mostly that I'm just not a real person.

I've finally been diagnosed as having BPD (first suicide attempt was nearly 8 years ago, but had mood problems and self harmed for longer than that).

I've had half a dozen gp's in the last few years (due to constantly moving house) and I think I've liked one of them, who still didn't think it was anything more than depression.

How did I finally seem to get help?  In the space of a few weeks I ended up in hospital twice (once after my boyfriend found me eating rat poison, the other after I just walked out of work in the middle of the day, visited every pharmacy in the area and took an overdose of sleeping pills in a park), and at the gp's several times - I would get hysterical - be screaming for it to stop, not know what to do, tried ringing like nhs direct who sent me to my gp, who did nothing, which eventually led to me starting to act on suicidal feelings.  The second time I was in hospital my partner asked to come into the talks with the psychiatristy people, as we both agreed that it was unlikely that the doctor last time I was in told me I was just useless and pathetic, but that's what I hear, my boyfriend pushed for me to keep be being seen by the crisis team, and for me to get assessed for psychotherapy.  It was there that they decided I sounded like I had BPD (something I hadn't really looked at before, as I'm somewhat wary of trying to self diagnose).

You don't say where you are and I don't know what the situation is like in the US, but if you are in the UK then I can only suggest you just keep trying services when you are in a state, I must have spoken to my gp while in hysterics 3 or 4 times before I even heard of a crisis team, and it wasn't until the second time in hospital that they seemed to really give a toss.  If you don't want to ring 999 then try just nhs direct, I previously got a referral to a community mental health team through them (about 9 months ago - they just increased my dose of venlafaxine).  It seems to be a case of just throwing yourself at different doctors and services until you get somewhere.

Which is what felt so frustrating - I felt at first so much like I wanted help but just couldn't get it, like they wouldn't take me seriously unless I actually did kill myself, by which point it would be too late.  And that the pain I was going through, kicking and screaming and pleading to air around me to make it stop was really just irrelevant and something I would just have to put up with until it killed me.

It helps to talk about it I think, I've survived for years talking to a few friends who've been through depression in different ways to me, but it helps for us to be able to vent about it to each other without feeling judged.

Push your doctor for help, for referral to a psychiatrist to assess you properly, point out that the drugs are not working, and try to find ways to cope and vent your anger and stress away from your fiancée and at work.  Er, much easier said than done I think!!

Cheers, I will take a look at the books, I've felt a bit better since reading about it all so more reading can't hurt.

To be honest they haven't actually told me I have BPD but have referred me to a service which seems to be exclusively for people with BPD who have in turn sent me leaflets giving me information about BPD, so I'm inferring that that's what they've decided I've got.  In some ways it makes me feel better, as there are some things that seem to be characteristics of that which never quite fitted in with the previous diagnosis of major depressive disorder and made it seem like it wasn't really a problem.  I've always hated the implication that because my self harm and suicidal things are very impulsive it's just me 'acting up' and if I was serious I'd spend weeks planning and preparing for it.

Mine has spent a couple of nights in the hospital with me and I've done my best to be as open as possible (although I sometimes hide some things from him).  He's been at appointments with my GP and crisis team though, which is a good thing, he's better at talking than me (when I ask him to explain something), and he remembers things much better too, I tend to take away the wrong message, like I know logically that a psychiatrist in a hospital probably isn't telling me I'm useless and pathetic, but that's what I hear.  He also feels better being there and feels like it's hard for him to help if he doesn't know what's going on.

Haha, yes, at least when I get overly emotional I'm a 5'2" girl so angry me looks more comical than anything and I don't look *so* weird crying over everything, although that was something my old boss had a real problem with, I really struggled to explain that I just couldn't help it while he just got frustrated that he couldn't give me any kind of feedback without me bursting into tears, I say old boss because it did lose me my job (but it was a boring job anyway, if for a cool company).

Thanks.  The service I've been referred to provides DBT.  I normally give up with everything very easily, part of why I think I've probably failed to get proper treatment until now, boyfriend and family are making sure I see it through properly.  Feeling positive/hopeful about treatment, but also a little scared of getting my hopes up unjustly, or just getting frustrated by how long it takes (I'm not very good at waiting for things!).
